item.subject: science
item.stem:
The diagram shows Farid's circuit: a cell, a switch, and a nichrome wire. He closes the switch so current flows for a short time.

Which claim correctly explains why the nichrome wire becomes warm?

options.A: Current through the wire meets resistance, so heat is produced and the wire feels warm.
options.B: The wire becomes warm first, and that warmth then makes the current start to flow.
options.C: Only nichrome becomes warm with current; a copper wire in the same circuit would never warm.
options.D: The wire becomes warm because the current's magnetic field heats the metal.
